newsitem.title: UK: Pearson denies talk of rift with TV boss.
newsitem.headline: Pearson denies talk of rift with TV boss.

text.p: Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino denied on Monday that she was at loggerheads with Greg Dyke, head of the company's TV arm.
"We are not having open warfare...It is just not true," Scardino told a news conference. "There was never an MBO proposal made that we rejected," she added.
Recent newspaper reports have said that Scardino and Dyke have fallen out after the chief executive rejected Dyke's attempts to lead a management buy out of the television business.
Scardino made it clear that she remained committed to television, pointing out that it was probably the company's highest growth business.

She said that Pearson was considering means of "giving scale" to a business that includes a 24 percent stake in Britain's new Channel 5 commercial TV station and an international programme production unit.
To underline the point, Pearson held its interim results presentation at its new TV headquarters in central London.
Dyke was not present on Monday morning. He is currently on holiday off the coast of Australia.
